note: Re-judged 2026-10-27 (independent judge, after 5935713168). RFC 7296 Section 2.23.1: "For transport mode, it MUST use exactly one IP address in the TSi and TSr payloads." and "It can have multiple Traffic Selectors if it has, for example, multiple port ranges that it wants to negotiate, but all TSi entries must use the IP1-IP1 range as the IP addresses, and all TSr entries must have the IPN2-IPN2 range as IP addresses." 5935713168 moved the floor/ceiling/one-pair doc comment from the IKE_AUTH wrapper narrowChildSelectors onto narrowChildSelectorsIn and renamed recordInitiatorSelectors to recordInitiatorSelectorsIn in two comments; the code of narrowChildSelectorsIn is unchanged (substitution, policy match, then for mode == modeTransport keepSingleAddress refusing an empty result with errTSUnacceptable and oneTransportPair), and the wrapper still passes decidedChildMode(sa). keepSingleAddress, oneTransportPair and transportSelectorPairs are unchanged, and no tagged unit changed. Initiator: transportSelectorPairs builds every proposed selector from the IKE SA's two observed addresses while ports and protocols survive, and TestTransportModeUsesExactlyOneAddress sweeps every TSi/TSr entry for start == end and requires the two port selectors to survive (the permitted multi-selector clause; its verified mutant record cuts transportSelectorPairs to one configured pair). Responder: the /16 refusal in that unit, reached through decideResponderTransportMode with a Fatal setup guard, discriminates the gate: commenting out keepSingleAddress in narrowChildSelectorsIn turns that unit red ("a transport-mode exchange accepted a /16 selector"), observed again this audit at 405f0fe639. TestResponderAnswersTheIKESAAddressesBehindANAT answers exactly one selector each, one address each, substituted to the observed addresses; its two revert records on substituteResponderSelectors verify. TestTransportChildRekeyAfterIKERekeyHoldsOneAddress is the positive half only, as tagged: a transport Child SA rekeyed after an IKE SA rekey answers one address in TSi and TSr and installs the one host pair in transport mode (verified mutant record on the rekey mode decision in respondChildRekey); under the keepSingleAddress mutant it stays green, observed this audit, because the Section 2.9.2 floor narrows a /24 to the retired host pair first, so no rekey-path negative of the gate exists and none is claimed. The new TestTransportChildRekeyAfterIKERekeyThroughSession (untagged) and TestChildRekeyWithoutTransportNotifyBehindNATIsRefused (Section 2.9.2 floor, AC-5) carry no 2.23.1-1 tag and are not counted. All tagged units PASS at 405f0fe639. Pre-existing labeling note, unchanged: the negative tag in TestTransportModeUsesExactlyOneAddress guards the permitted multi-selector clause rather than a violating input; the violating-input negatives are the /16 refusal in the same unit and the NAT responder's substituted answer.
